reviews.Author: kingcola
reviews.OriginDescription: Reviewed in the United States on November 19, 2020
reviews.Text: This is just chunks of salt, like coarse salt from Morton only somewhat smaller chunks. No flakiness going on here. I didn't want chunks, I wanted flakes, so I returned it. Then I ordered the Maldon sea salt flakes and they are actually flakes. The Maldon costs a little less than this brand and you get a half ounce more. The Maldon packaging is not as good --it's a sealed plastic bag of salt inside a cardboard box, you have to cut the plastic bag open to get the salt out and there's not an ideal way to close the bag except just to fold it over and maybe put a piece of tape on it and keep it in the box. No convenient pour spout like with the SaltWorks brand. But I want salt flakes first, so I don't really care that this brand has better packaging, it certainly doesn't have better salt.
reviews.Title: Not flakes ...chunks

reviews.Author: Sharon Farage
reviews.OriginDescription: Reviewed in the United States on September 22, 2020
reviews.Text: Very disappointed with the product. False advertisement the description states produced from the Pacific Ocean. Received the product today and on the package it states produced in South Korea. The Pacific isn’t close to them. Shame on you Kosher Flake Sea Salt Perfect for baking, cooking and finishing, Pacific Blue is an all-natural kosher flake sea salt that is produced from the Pacific Ocean. This variety delivers all of the beneficial nutrients of sea salt while retaining the treasured kosher flake texture. Unrefined and free of additives, the light, small flakes of Pacific Blue add great flavor when sprinkled on salads, added to baked goods, stirred into soups or paired with seafood and meat.
